bc_sugarloaf.blurb: Sugarloaf is one of the named cliffs inside Murrin Park, set right off Highway 99 between Britannia Beach and Squamish. The cliff is short, with lines of roughly 8 to 22 metres, and holds a couple dozen routes. Most are trad, with a handful of top-rope options, running from easy beginner lines through the middle grades up to a few 5.11s and a 5.12. Because the top is reachable on foot and the easy lines are simple to rig, it works well as a first outing for newer climbers learning to set anchors, while stronger leaders can still find a challenge on the harder cracks and faces.
bc_sugarloaf.approach: From the main lot, follow the trail starting beside the toilet building at the south end. It curves uphill for a few minutes to the cliff base. To reach the top, continue around the right side of the cliff.

bc_cereal_killers.blurb: Cereal Killers is a small crag in Murrin Park near Squamish, a short stroll west of the lower part of Pet Wall, off the loop trail that heads toward the park's western edge. It holds a dozen or so routes mixing sport and trad, and the climbing is mostly in the 5.10 range, with a few 5.8s, a handful of 5.11s and a 5.12. Styles vary from easy-to-moderate lines to very technical vertical slab. A standard Squamish trad rack, small wires through large cams, covers the gear lines. Several cleaned projects at the right end await ascents.
